findings: The finite minimum includes the explicit cap. A result strictly below it is attained by a genuine allowed native walk within the horizon; every allowed bounded walk supplies the converse upper bound. Materialized vector rows retain the previous horizon once in the recurrence.

The 0/1 entry charge plus initial covered label equals the actual distinct chain-set cardinality because the existing fixed-source filter gives no reentry. Tail rebasing is used only for validity, in the proved forward direction; it never asserts hereditary minimum distances.

The horizon n and cap n+1 are justified by legal augmentation preserving DAG acyclicity, hence actual simple paths of length below n. The original-unreachable case cannot produce a nonsentinel allowed walk. The existing zero convention is applied only after testing the sentinel, preserving covered/uncovered self pairs.

Original reachability is computed from supplied Boolean adjacency. Unique chain labels, least reachable chain indices, entry vertices, the actual fixed-source filter and original important demands are constructed and proved equal to the existing definitions.
The final objective and stopping theorems identify the literal original potential and stopped predicate under legal H; they do not substitute an excess-normalized, hereditary, or unrelated objective.
scope_limits: The original Boolean adjacency must represent the context graph; the finite chain nodes and preprocessing witnesses/data remain supplied. Their extraction from a raw graph is not constructed here.
There is no physical runtime, allocation or bit-operation theorem. In particular, the repeated reachability/filter evaluations and finite data enumerations are not covered by a global time bound.
No executable raw-greedy maximizing selector, complete preprocessing algorithm, or full Algorithm2 runtime/cubic progress theorem follows from this dependency packet.
